f326e951ae509389: Which Indian city has the most craft breweries?

822c3125ac699eec: What is the difference between a brewpub and a microbrewery?
f109dbf3af3bc476: A brewpub brews beer on site and serves it there, usually with food. A microbrewery is a small brewery that may package or supply beer beyond its own premises. Licence categories and names differ by state.
596176751a479f06: How do I get a brewery added or corrected?

f1f3de64ebdca3e3: Brewing Glossary: Beer Terms Explained | Craft Beer School
cd4b71f20e785961: 295 brewing, tasting, packaging, business and wine terms, defined in plain English for brewers and drinkers in India. Search, filter by topic or jump to a letter.
18db6828d508a006: Share of a beer's volume that is ethanol, shown as a percentage. Brewers estimate it from gravity readings with ABV = (OG - FG) x 131.25, using specific gravity. Read the guideAlso: Alcohol by volume
9c03d7f7b98c9c3a: Green apple compound yeast makes on the way to alcohol and normally reabsorbs. Noticeable levels point to beer pulled off yeast too early, under-pitching or oxidation. Read the guide
df5dcb43b53dab5d: Malt carrying lactic acid from lactic bacteria grown on it during malting. A few per cent of the grist lowers mash pH into range without adding mineral acid. Read the guideAlso: Sauermalz
770c11d796ec7ec2: Any unmalted source of fermentable sugar, such as rice, maize or sugar, used alongside malt. Adjuncts lighten body and flavour, lower cost and are common in Indian mainstream lagers. Read the guide
995829f56f02112b: Number on a whisky label giving the age of the youngest spirit in the bottle. A 12-year-old can contain older whisky but nothing younger. Read the guide
f7b6dcf6d001b1d8: Beer fermented with top-fermenting ale yeast at warmer temperatures, often 15 to 22°C (59 to 72°F). Ales tend to show more fruity esters than lagers. Read the guide
5f9dfcab4ad490af: Strains of Saccharomyces cerevisiae that ferment warm, typically 15 to 24 °C (59 to 75 °F), producing fruity esters. Many rise to the top during fermentation, hence the old name top-fermenting yeast. Read the guideAlso: Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Top-fermenting yeast
07ccee6af51ab941: Ability of water to resist a drop in pH, mainly from bicarbonate, expressed as mg/L of calcium carbonate. High alkalinity pushes mash pH up, which suits dark beers more than pale ones. Read the guideAlso: Total alkalinity
8812aa93f92a4fd0: Resins in hop lupulin that become bitter once isomerised in the boil. The alpha acid percentage on a hop packet is how brewers calculate the dose for a target bitterness. Read the guideAlso: Humulones
21c8acac0e74531f: Mash enzyme that chops starch chains at random points, most active around 68 to 72 °C (154 to 162 °F). It liquefies starch quickly, leaving dextrins as well as fermentable sugars. Read the guide
6ff053f7ec4aa0c7: Spirit lost to evaporation through the cask during maturation. Losses are far higher in hot climates such as India than in Scotland, which speeds ageing but costs volume. Read the guide
54c80361da25de94: What a beer smells like, sensed through the nose before and while drinking. Most of what people call taste is really aroma, so judges assess it first. Read the guide
661ad0543d8777f1: Dry, puckering, tea-like roughness on the palate caused by tannins and other polyphenols. A little suits some roasty beers; too much usually points to harsh husk extraction. Read the guide
242cbff165e26942: Drop in gravity during fermentation, shown as a percentage of the original gravity. Most brewing strains land roughly between 65 and 85 per cent, which shapes body and dryness. Read the guideAlso: Apparent attenuation
0c5191338353e6fd: Beer matured in wooden barrels, often ex-bourbon, wine or rum, picking up vanilla, oak, spirit or wine notes. Ageing takes months and the wood can host souring microbes. Read the guide
2036eeb851e5b092: Pale, highly enzymatic malt such as pilsner or pale ale malt that makes up most of a grist. It provides the bulk of the fermentable extract plus the enzymes to convert it. Read the guide
4321c56969177c55: Printed code on a can, bottle or keg that ties it to a brew, tank and packaging run. Without it a recall or complaint investigation becomes guesswork. Read the guideAlso: lot code
42e495d2ac79fa75: Volume lost between brewhouse and sale through tank bottoms, filling waste, breakages and dumped batches. Tracking it stage by stage is one of the cheapest profit gains. Read the guideAlso: yield loss
353a985e6c53a6e9: Low-strength, very pale, sharply tart wheat beer from Berlin, often around 3% ABV. It was traditionally served with flavoured syrups to soften the acidity. Read the guide
057dca7be4f86809: Best before date Packaging and quality
5da3ff4e407d2fc4: Date on a label up to which the producer expects the drink to keep its quality when stored as directed. It is a quality promise, not a safety cut-off. Read the guide
a5f05c2298957b8e: Hop resins that barely isomerise in the boil, so they add little bitterness at first. They can oxidise over time into bitter compounds and they have antibacterial activity. Read the guideAlso: Lupulones
3e2faf9a57517ec5: Mash enzyme that snips maltose from the ends of starch chains, most active around 60 to 65 °C (140 to 149 °F). It is heat sensitive, so cooler mashes give drier, more fermentable worts. Read the guide
d6f2462a35dc4d69: Rest around 35 to 45 °C (95 to 113 °F) where beta-glucanase breaks down gums from grain cell walls. It eases lautering in grists high in oats, rye or unmalted barley. Read the guide
08000b5d682ace9c: Enzyme that breaks down beta-glucans, the sticky gums in grain cell walls. Without enough of it wort turns viscous, lautering slows and beer can haze or filter poorly. Read the guide
b8c751e268e7ae00: Chemical changes yeast makes to hop compounds during fermentation, such as converting geraniol or freeing bound thiols. It is why dry hopping during active fermentation tastes different from dry hopping afterwards. Read the guide
f039813a8ec17093: Lab measure of bitterness made by extracting acidified beer with iso-octane and reading absorbance at 275 nm. It tracks bitter hop compounds, not how bitter a beer actually tastes. Read the guideAlso: BU, IBU measurement
8b59d6245c6e1f4e: US non-profit that writes widely used beer style guidelines and certifies beer judges through tasting exams. Its guidelines are the reference at most homebrew competitions. Read the guideAlso: Beer Judge Certification Program
a52da5baad06720b: Whisky made by mixing different whiskies, typically malt and grain. Many Indian blends also include neutral spirit, which is why labels and definitions differ by market. Read the guide
fe024ed2fb7103e7: Strong German lager, roughly 6 to 7.5% ABV, with rich toasty malt and little hop character. Doppelbock, maibock and eisbock are stronger or seasonal relatives. Read the guide
7ebefdc3813dca9d: Perceived weight or fullness of a beer on the palate, from thin and watery to thick and chewy. Residual sugars, proteins and alcohol all add to it. Read the guide
9ffe05b6b2cdd3f7: Vigorous boiling of the wort, usually for 60 to 90 minutes. It sterilises the wort, isomerises hop acids, drives off DMS and coagulates protein. Read the guideAlso: Wort boiling
da11228e154f0459: Store where alcohol is held under excise supervision before duty is paid. Duty usually falls due as stock leaves bond, though procedures vary by state. Read the guide
fcdaa5a571d54ad3: Glass container for beer, most often brown because amber glass blocks most of the light that causes skunky flavour. Green and clear glass give little protection. Read the guide
75fb01cd7aad66f3: Carbonating beer in the bottle with a small dose of priming sugar plus live yeast. It leaves a fine yeast sediment and the yeast helps mop up oxygen. Read the guide
12b8fc6991563b87: Volume of wort a brewhouse can produce per brew, usually given in hectolitres. Annual output also depends on brews per day and how much fermenting space follows. Read the guide
ea5040a7922f95e6: Share of the malt's potential extract that reaches the fermenter as wort. It is how breweries judge milling, mashing and lautering, since losses show up as wasted malt. Read the guide
09c18599c7d34309: Simple sugars such as sucrose, dextrose or invert sugar added in the kettle to raise alcohol without adding body. Belgian brewers use them to keep strong beers dry and drinkable. Read the guideAlso: Dextrose, Candi sugar
e72dc69c969282c3: Restaurant or bar that brews beer on site and serves it there, usually straight from serving tanks. In several Indian states it is the main craft beer model. Read the guide
b55c0ac45af37b56: Bright beer tank Fermentation and conditioning
a7ae1ec9ca3d7fe4: Pressure-rated tank that holds finished, clarified beer ready for packaging or serving. In brewpubs beer is often poured straight from it.Also: BBT, Serving tank
420861950b6e7515: Sugar concentration scale read on refractometers, close to Plato for unfermented wort. Once alcohol is present, refractometer readings need a correction formula.Also: Degrees Brix
b3efc443af098669: Volume of a drink as measured, whatever its strength. Indian excise often counts beer in bulk litres and spirits in proof litres; methods vary by state. Read the guideAlso: BL
a2dfa775bc2dc391: Most important brewing mineral, lowering mash pH, protecting enzymes and helping yeast settle. Many brewers aim for at least 50 mg/L in their brewing water. Read the guide
b949ad439f6cb2ba: Aluminium container with a thin inner lining, sealed by a lid seamed onto the body. Cans block all light and weigh little, though filling must be tightly controlled to keep oxygen out. Read the guide
76e134dbe0cdac72: Carbon dioxide dissolved in beer, giving fizz, lift to aroma and a livelier mouthfeel. Its level is set by temperature and pressure, whether produced naturally or forced in. Read the guide
7a5e42ce2723e720: Prickly, slightly acidic tingle on the tongue as dissolved CO2 forms carbonic acid. Higher carbonation makes beer feel lighter and sharper; low carbonation feels softer and fuller. Read the guideAlso: carbonation perception
1d033a15f1ef93b1: Standard selling unit of packaged drinks, such as 12 bottles of 650 ml or 24 cans of 500 ml. Case sizes differ, so convert to litres before comparing sales. Read the guide
51e5e10532d32d7c: Wooden container, usually oak, used to mature spirits and wine. Ex-bourbon and ex-sherry casks are the most common for whisky, each shaping colour and flavour. Read the guideAlso: barrel
94f758ee2d70c86a: Unfiltered ale that finishes conditioning in its cask and is served without added gas pressure, usually by hand pump. Once tapped it must be sold within days because air replaces the beer drawn off.Also: real ale
12cf1b6999dbdf27: Whisky bottled at the strength it comes out of the cask, without dilution with water, often above 50% ABV. Read the guideAlso: barrel proof
815db4a6517dcf8d: Machine spinning beer at high speed so yeast and solids are thrown out by centrifugal force. It clarifies quickly with little beer loss, useful for hazy beers that need partial clarity. Read the guide
3900cb7c3b503168: Separate vessel that boils rice or maize with a little malt to gelatinise the starch before it joins the main mash. It is standard kit in breweries that brew with rice or maize grits. Read the guideAlso: Adjunct cooker
6b71d98595d66931: Cloudiness that appears when beer is cold and clears as it warms, caused by protein and polyphenol complexes. Over time it can turn into permanent haze. Read the guide
d84fc1a74437ef26: Certification programme for beer service and knowledge, running from Certified Beer Server up to Master Cicerone. It focuses on serving, storing, styles and food pairing. Read the guide
7083fdcbbd839acb: Cleaning tanks and pipes by pumping hot caustic, acid and rinse water through fixed spray balls and lines without taking them apart. It is the backbone of brewery hygiene. Read the guideAlso: Cleaning in place
8676fbd6702aad67: Removing soil, protein, beer stone and other deposits from a surface, usually with caustic or acid detergents. A surface must be clean before it can be sanitised. Read the guide
426e4a2f87357b65: Cleaning in place Packaging and quality
cef59d9836e8b085: Cleaning tanks and pipework by pumping detergent and rinse cycles through them without taking them apart. Time, temperature, concentration and flow together decide whether it works. Read the guideAlso: CIP
beb902551b9fcd07: Direct cost of making the product sold: ingredients, packaging, direct labour and production overheads. Companies treat excise differently within it, so check before comparing figures. Read the guideAlso: cost of goods sold
f6e82be627f661c3: One of the main alpha acid analogues, usually quoted as a percentage of total alpha acids. Many brewers believe high-cohumulone hops give a harsher bitterness, though the evidence is debated. Read the guide
2f15824e0d95ef08: Fine protein and polyphenol particles that drop out of wort when it is chilled quickly. Fast cooling improves it, giving clearer beer. Read the guide
26e896c885ce4842: Rapidly chilling finished beer to near 0 °C (32 °F) to drop yeast, protein and hop particles out of suspension. It speeds clarity before packaging or filtration. Read the guideAlso: Crash cooling
e92d552614fde19c: Crisp, dry IPA fermented with lager yeast at warmer temperatures, often with rice or maize in the grist. It pairs West Coast hop character with lager cleanness. Read the guide
1b93eba8fc563dd6: Tall still that distils continuously over many internal plates, producing a lighter, stronger spirit efficiently. It is used for grain whisky, vodka and most Indian molasses spirit. Read the guideAlso: continuous still, Coffey still
f59baf8d19fa53be: Period after primary fermentation when beer matures, clears and carbonates. Yeast cleans up off-flavours such as diacetyl and acetaldehyde during this time. Read the guideAlso: Maturation, Secondary
ac144280f04a0080: Arrangement where a brand owner pays an established brewery to brew and package its recipe. It lets brands launch without building a plant, though quality depends on the host. Read the guide
4dcd9246944dcac3: Time-ordered plot of a measurement with a centre line and statistical control limits. Points outside the limits or unusual runs show a process has shifted and needs attention. Read the guide
acf1f7a11d2f5c02: Musty, damp cardboard smell caused by trichloroanisole, often from a contaminated cork. Even tiny amounts mute a wine's fruit. Read the guideAlso: TCA
3a0f2aa7d9fb2d7b: Cost per litre Business and India
d5b4b1c350dc4228: Total cost of making one litre of finished beer, including ingredients, packaging, energy, labour and overheads. Pricing and margin decisions should start from this number. Read the guide
8b1068173134f5fd: Beer from smaller, independent breweries that prize flavour, variety and local character. India has no single legal definition, so the term is used loosely. Read the guide
1a39663b28797f28: Crimped metal cap that seals a beer bottle, with a liner that grips the glass. Some liners absorb oxygen, which helps slow staling in the bottle.Also: crown cork, crown cap
cd368347600dd4be: Lupulin separated from cone material at very low temperature, then pelletised, giving roughly twice the resin content of standard pellets. Less leafy matter means less beer lost to hop debris. Read the guideAlso: Lupulin powder, Lupulin pellets
ac010234eef9260e: Speciality malt stewed while wet so its starch turns to sugar inside the husk before kilning or roasting. It adds sweetness, body plus caramel to toffee flavours, with colour set by how hard it is roasted. Read the guideAlso: Caramel malt
bbe1ba8b312f0a21: Moments when a distiller switches the spirit run from heads to hearts and from hearts to tails. Only the hearts are kept, so cut timing shapes flavour. Read the guideAlso: heads, hearts and tails
1a99f484767aed55: Tall fermenter with a cone at the base where yeast and trub collect. It is standard in modern breweries because yeast is easy to remove and harvest.Also: CCT, Fermentation vessel, FV
5c3fef083055562a: Mash method where part of the mash is drawn off, boiled then returned to raise the temperature. It deepens malt flavour and colour, the traditional route for many German and Czech lagers. Read the guideAlso: Decoction
e15f6134ce1ce6d2: Brewing scale giving the percentage by weight of dissolved extract in wort or beer, so 12°P means 12 g of extract per 100 g of liquid. Most commercial breweries record gravity this way. Read the guideAlso: °P, Plato
977661269acd89e7: Volume a distributor sells on to retailers and bars, a closer signal of real demand than brewery shipments. Comparing the two shows stock building up or running down in the trade. Read the guide
10299bf9ef125cb8: Longer chains of glucose that most brewing yeast cannot ferment. They stay in the beer as body with a little sweetness; higher mash temperatures leave more of them. Read the guide
e21389f02648eb62: Buttery, butterscotch compound formed from a yeast by-product during fermentation. Healthy yeast reabsorbs it if given time, so high levels usually mean rushed fermentation or infection. Read the guide
54e8cbc30a4c9c75: Warming beer a few degrees near the end of fermentation, often to around 16 to 18 °C (61 to 64 °F) for lagers, so yeast clears diacetyl faster. It is standard before lagering. Read the guide
341196b9a9f97d6b: Measure of the starch-converting enzyme activity in a malt, given in degrees Lintner or WK. It tells you whether a grist has enough enzymes to convert adjuncts and speciality malts. Read the guideAlso: DP
dd1ad6bd68d00ec5: STA1-positive variant of brewing yeast that slowly ferments dextrins and starch. In packaged beer it causes over-carbonation, gushing and burst bottles, so breweries treat it as a serious contaminant. Read the guideAlso: Saccharomyces cerevisiae var. diastaticus
6fd8e4b9f6036468: Powdered fossil algae used as a filter aid, building a porous cake that traps yeast and haze. It works well but needs careful handling because the dust harms lungs. Read the guideAlso: DE, Kieselguhr
df5778c3bf789ca0: Oxygen dissolved in finished beer, usually measured in parts per billion. Keeping it low after fermentation is the biggest single guard against stale flavours. Read the guideAlso: DO
17ecb26543899c5c: Sulphur compound tasting of cooked sweetcorn, formed from SMM in pale malt when wort is heated. A vigorous, uncovered boil drives it off; slow chilling lets more form. Read the guideAlso: Dimethyl sulphide
33d42f8c5317036a: Stronger, more intensely hopped IPA, typically around 7.5 to 10% ABV. It needs extra malt to carry the hops without tasting harsh. Read the guideAlso: DIPA, imperial IPA
3618a3ebc2d135c1: Draught line cleaning Packaging and quality
e8f101e6d2bd82a1: Regular flushing of beer lines, couplers and taps with line cleaner to remove yeast, bacteria and scale. Dirty lines are a common reason good beer tastes bad at the bar. Read the guideAlso: line cleaning
2dfba7a42e687c2e: Day when the sale of alcohol is banned, such as certain national holidays, election days and some festivals. State governments set the dates, so taprooms plan stock and staff around them. Read the guide
fdca07e7ee9ecccd: Adding hops to beer during or after fermentation for aroma without much extra bitterness. Timing, dose and contact time all shape the result. Read the guide
f4022bd6b397077e: State where the sale and consumption of alcohol is prohibited, wholly or largely. Prohibition policies change over time, so check the current position state by state. Read the guide
d77388edadb4f7f0: European Brewery Convention scale for beer and malt colour, read from light absorbance at 430 nm. EBC values are roughly double SRM values, which helps when comparing recipes. Read the guideAlso: EBC
